formats.character_rule: 'Direct Address' is one person speaking straight to the viewer — set Characters to 1.
formats.details: One speaker talks straight to the viewer, looking into the camera — a personal, to-camera address.
formats.name: Direct Address
formats.style_directive:
FORMAT DIRECTIVE: DIRECT ADDRESS:
- ONE speaker talks straight into the camera as if speaking to a friend — intimate, first-person voice.
- Structure: hook → build → payoff. Open with a striking line, develop the news, land a memorable closer.
- Rhetorical questions are welcome as setups; answer them with real facts from the news.
- Keep every line inside the speaker's world — they talk about the news, not about the video.
formats.dialogue_directive:
DIALOGUE TYPE: DIRECT ADDRESS (one speaker, intimate direct-to-camera)
- ONLY {A} speaks — every single beat, looking straight into the lens. This is PERSONAL, not a public rally.
- Speak to the viewer as a confidant: open with a hook, use rhetorical questions as setups, land punchy payoffs.
- First-person voice ('main aapko bata raha hoon...'). No crowd, no second voice, nobody answering back.

formats.character_rule: 'Normal Talk' needs at least 2 people talking to each other naturally.
formats.details: Two or more people have a natural, everyday conversation about the news — relaxed and relatable.
formats.name: Normal Talk
formats.style_directive:
FORMAT DIRECTIVE: NORMAL TALK:
- This is a natural, everyday conversation between the characters about the news!
- Characters speak back-and-forth, reacting to each other's words, questioning, and keeping it relatable.
- Keep every line inside the characters' world — they talk to each other about the news.
formats.dialogue_directive:
DIALOGUE TYPE: NATURAL CONVERSATION
- Two people talking like real friends — relaxed, reactive ping-pong.
- Balance humor with the verified news facts; every joke must come from a real fact.

formats.character_rule: 'Q&A' needs a host plus at least 1 guest answering the questions.
formats.details: A host asks sharp, engaging questions; the guest answers with exciting, funny, or deep revelations.
formats.name: Q&A
formats.style_directive:
FORMAT DIRECTIVE: Q&A:
- The host asks sharp, engaging questions; the guest responds with exciting, funny, or deep revelations.
- Questions must dig into the news — no softballs. Answers carry the facts with personality.
- Keep every line inside the characters' world — they talk to each other about the news.
formats.dialogue_directive:
DIALOGUE TYPE: Q&A (strict host-and-guest)
- {A} is the HOST: asks ONLY sharp, short questions. Every host line MUST end with '?'.
- {B} is the GUEST: answers using the verified facts. The guest NEVER asks a question (no '?' in guest lines).
- Beat order is law: odd beats (1, 3, 5) = host question; even beats (2, 4) = guest answer. No exceptions.

formats.character_rule: 'Debate' needs at least 2 opposing sides arguing it out.
formats.details: Two opposing sides clash over the news — claim, rebuttal, and witty counter-points.
formats.name: Debate
formats.style_directive:
FORMAT DIRECTIVE: DEBATE:
- Two opposing viewpoints clash with witty counter-points, lively banter, and engaging arguments.
- Structure every exchange as claim → rebuttal → counter. Nobody concedes easily.
- Ground the clash in real stakes from the news; end with a sharp verdict or twist.
- Keep every line inside the characters' world — they debate the news itself.
formats.dialogue_directive:
DIALOGUE TYPE: DEBATE (structured for-vs-against)
- {A} DEFENDS the news development; {B} ATTACKS it. Sides NEVER swap, NEVER agree.
- ONE speaker per beat. Beats strictly alternate: {A}, {B}, {A}, {B}, ...
- Beat 1 ({A}): bold opening claim built on one verified fact.
- Every later beat must FIRST directly rebut the previous beat's point, THEN add its own claim or fact.
- Final beat: knockout verdict line for your side. No neutral filler, no changing the subject.

formats.character_rule: 'Interrogation' needs an interrogator plus 1–2 people being questioned.
formats.details: Tough, probing questions press for the truth — an investigative grilling that peels back layers.
formats.name: Interrogation
formats.style_directive:
FORMAT DIRECTIVE: INTERROGATION:
- One character grills the other(s) with tough, probing questions — an investigative press for the truth.
- Questions escalate: start curious, get sharper. The questioned character deflects, then cracks or reveals.
- Every answer must surface a real fact from the news.
- Keep every line inside the characters' world — they talk to each other about the news.
formats.dialogue_directive:
DIALOGUE TYPE: INTERROGATION (grilling for the truth)
- {A} is the INTERROGATOR: asks ONLY tough, probing questions. Every interrogator line MUST end with '?'.
- {B} is the SUBJECT: answers, deflects, then reveals — using the verified facts. The subject NEVER asks a question (no '?' in subject lines).
- Beat order is law: odd beats (1, 3, 5) = interrogator question; even beats (2, 4) = subject answer. Questions escalate in intensity.

formats.character_rule: 'Reaction' works with 1–6 characters reacting to the news.
formats.details: Characters react to the news as it breaks — shock, disbelief, hot takes, and running commentary.
formats.name: Reaction
formats.style_directive:
FORMAT DIRECTIVE: REACTION:
- Characters react to the news as it unfolds — genuine shock, disbelief, hot takes, running commentary.
- Reactions must be big and speakable: gasps, exclamations, instant opinions, relatable comparisons to everyday life.
- Anchor every reaction to a real news beat.
- Keep every line inside the characters' world — they react to the news together.
formats.dialogue_directive:
DIALOGUE TYPE: REACTION (live responses to the news)
- Characters react to the news as it breaks — shock, disbelief, hot takes, running commentary.
- Big, speakable reactions anchored to real news beats; every reaction must come from a verified fact.

formats.character_rule: 'Thinking Out Loud' is 1–2 voices reasoning through the news aloud.
formats.details: A reflective voice reasons through the news aloud — thinking it through in real time, step by step.
formats.name: Thinking Out Loud
formats.style_directive:
FORMAT DIRECTIVE: THINKING OUT LOUD:
- A reflective voice works through the news aloud in real time — wondering, weighing, connecting dots.
- Use natural thought-speech: 'wait, so that means…', self-questions answered aloud.
- The thinking must LAND somewhere: a conclusion, a realisation, a decision.
- Keep every line inside the thinker's world — they work through the news aloud.
formats.dialogue_directive:
DIALOGUE TYPE: THINKING OUT LOUD (reasoning aloud)
- A reflective voice works through the news in real time — wondering, weighing, connecting dots aloud.
- Natural thought-speech with self-questions answered aloud; the thinking must LAND on a conclusion or a sharp question.

formats.character_rule: 'Secret-Sharing' is 1–2 voices sharing the inside story confidentially.
formats.details: A confessional, hush-hush tone — 'come close, here's what really happened' insider energy.
formats.name: Secret-Sharing
formats.style_directive:
FORMAT DIRECTIVE: SECRET-SHARING:
- Confessional, hush-hush energy — 'come close, let me tell you what really happened.'
- The speaker shares the news like insider knowledge: lowered voice, conspiratorial asides, 'nobody is telling you this' framing.
- Every 'secret' must be grounded in the verified news.
- Keep every line inside the speaker's world — they share the news directly.
formats.dialogue_directive:
DIALOGUE TYPE: SECRET-SHARING (confessional insider telling)
- Hush-hush, confessional energy — 'here is what really happened', told like insider knowledge.
- Every 'secret' must be grounded in the verified news facts; dramatise the telling, never the facts.

formats.character_rule: 'Drama' needs 2 to 4 characters in direct emotional conflict or dramatic scene reenactment.
formats.details: High-stakes dramatic confrontation or theatrical reenactment of the news with emotional tension, pauses, and character stakes.
formats.name: Drama
formats.style_directive:
FORMAT DIRECTIVE: DRAMA:
- High-stakes, theatrical interpersonal conflict or cinematic reenactment inspired by the news!
- Characters don't just chat — their personal stakes, convictions, or livelihoods clash directly.
- Include dramatic pauses, emotional reactions, and escalating tension before a turning point or revelation.
- Ground the drama 100% in verified news facts; dramatise character reactions and personal impact, NEVER invent false news claims.
- Keep every line inside the scene world — characters live the situation, they do not present a news report.
formats.dialogue_directive:
DIALOGUE TYPE: DRAMATIC SCENE (theatrical conflict & high stakes)
- Characters clash over real consequences of the news — tension, defensiveness, sharp comebacks, and emotional gravity.
- Use dramatic pacing: short, sharp confrontations alternating with weight and tension.
- Audio and SFX should use subtle dramatic beats, tense ambience, or sudden silence — no light comedic effects.
- Conclude with a dramatic turning point, harsh reality check, or emotional revelation.
